audit.why: Emerald+ headline 52.69% over 484 games; EVEN at 6/10 with a 7/10 carry threat is consistent.

audit.whatIsWrong: The last three rows disagree between layers. The content chart and packet levelChart read Skill / Rumble / Rumble / Skill / Cho'Gath / Skill / Cho'Gath; CHAMP_FULL.phases reads Skill / Rumble / Rumble / Skill / Skill / Rumble / Rumble. The full layer never gives Cho'Gath a single row, including the 2+ items row that the content layer's own late paragraph calls unwinnable.
audit.why: The content reasoning is right and follows the kit: Rumble owns 2-3 because Cho'Gath has no dash and must walk through a 600-range cone, level 6 goes to Cho'Gath on Feast, and stacked Feast health plus tank items makes a percentage-based magic-damage kit progressively less relevant. A chart that ends Rumble/Rumble contradicts the paragraph directly beneath it.
audit.corrected: phases[4], phases[5] and phases[6] side values all need changing and none fits the length band — Skill to Cho'Gath and Rumble to Cho'Gath are both well over 10 percent. Recorded in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feast is named as the level-6 spike and the cooldown to track in fourteen strings, and its cooldown appears nowhere.
audit.why: Feast is 80/70/60 — unusually short for an ultimate, and short enough that 'wait it out' is a much weaker plan than the text implies. A Rumble player who assumes a 120-second ultimate window will walk into the second one. Rumble's own spikes at 2-3, 4-5 and first item are correctly placed.
audit.corrected: 80 seconds at rank 1 written into the win condition, the cooldown breakdown, the Do and the level-6 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: The headline advice is backwards. The full layer says 'build MR' in the TL;DR, the win condition, and a Do literally titled 'Build MR for his R'. Feast deals true damage — magic resist does not reduce it at all. MR is worth buying against Feral Scream and Vorpal Spikes, but the ability the reader is told to buy it for is the one it does nothing against. Separately, Feral Scream's silence is the interaction that actually ends Rumble's trades and it is only glanced at: at 300 range it shuts off Flamespitter, Scrap Shield and Electro Harpoon at once, and Rumble is a champion who already spends part of every rotation silenced by his own Overheat.
audit.why: Riot's Feast text is 'dealing a high amount of true damage', and _missing-interactions.json independently flags this matchup with 'Cho'Gath bypasses stacking resistances (Feast) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here'. Stacking MR and then dying to Feast anyway is the exact failure this page should prevent. The Feral Scream point matters because a silenced Rumble cannot shield, and Scrap Shield is his only defensive tool.
audit.corrected: MR re-pointed at Feral Scream and Vorpal Spikes with Feast's true damage stated explicitly, in the TL;DR, win condition, cooldown breakdown, both relevant Dos, the silence Don't and the Key Ability Interactions row.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Cho'Gath cooldown appears in either layer.
audit.why: Feast 80/70/60, Feral Scream 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, Rupture a flat 6, Vorpal Spikes 8/7/6/5/4. Rupture at 6 seconds is worth knowing precisely because the text tells you to sidestep it — it comes back almost immediately, so dodging one is not a window.
audit.corrected: Real numbers added to the cooldown breakdown and the Rupture Don't.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid paragraph attributes Cho'Gath's lane sustain to 'his Vorpal Spikes healing'. Vorpal Spikes does not heal — it is damage and a slow off his attacks. His healing is Carnivore, the passive, which restores health and mana whenever he kills a unit.
audit.why: The distinction is actionable in opposite directions. If the heal came from Vorpal Spikes it would be tied to him attacking you, and trading less would reduce it. Because it is Carnivore, it is tied to him last-hitting, so the counter is denying him minions — freezing and zoning — not avoiding trades. wants.foe[2] also contains the duplicated typo 'Warmog's passive passive regeneration'.
audit.corrected: Sustain re-attributed to Carnivore in the mid paragraph and in Cho'Gath's wants; the doubled word removed.

At level 6 the dynamic shifts: Feast grants him a burst of true-damage HP that ignores your poke investment and his engage threat becomes real. Use Equalizer at 6 not as a duel tool but as a zoning wall across his escape path — cut him off with the rocket line and let the DoT do work while you stay out of Feast range. Avoid letting him chunk you low enough to be a Feast target.

Use The Equalizer as a zoning line across his approach, not as a duel tool, and stay outside Feral Scream's 300 range — silenced, you have no shield and no cone.

notes: The 'build MR' advice against Cho'Gath is the clearest actionable error in this matchup — the full layer has a Do titled 'Build MR for his R' and Feast is true damage. MR is still correct in this lane, just for Feral Scream and Vorpal Spikes, so I re-pointed it rather than removing it. Two smaller things. Rupture carries a 'grounding' derived flag in the kit file, but Riot's description says only knock-up, damage and slow, so I did not write grounding anywhere. And Vorpal Spikes carries no heal in its description while the mid paragraph credited it with one; Cho'Gath's sustain is Carnivore off unit kills, which changes the counter from 'trade less' to 'deny farm'. Unfixable within the band: phases[4], phases[5] and phases[6] all contradict the level chart, and notably the full layer awards Rumble the 2+ items row while the content late paragraph says the late 1v1 is unwinnable. suspectNames flagged 'Use Equalizer' — false positive.
